biography: Laurens Vanthoor, a name synonymous with relentless aggression and unwavering determination, hails from Hasselt, Belgium. His journey began not on the grand circuits of Europe, but on the local karting tracks, fueled by his father's own passion for motorsport. A defining moment came early in his career during a Formula Renault race at Spa-Francorchamps. Battling for the lead in treacherous conditions, Vanthoor executed a daring overtake around the outside of Eau Rouge, a move that cemented his reputation as a fearless competitor. After a successful career in GT racing, including winning the FIA GT World Championship in 2013, he has transitioned to Porsche's GTE program, becoming a linchpin of their factory effort. Despite some near misses at Le Mans, he continues to strive for that elusive victory, pushing himself and his team to the absolute limit.
drivingStyle: Vanthoor's driving style is characterized by aggressive precision. He's known for late braking maneuvers and an uncanny ability to extract maximum performance from his car, often flirting with the edge of grip. While naturally aggressive, Vanthoor has matured to incorporate tire management into his repertoire. He's able to push hard early in a stint to gain track position, then conserve tires effectively to maintain his advantage. His calm demeanor under pressure allows him to consistently deliver strong results, even when faced with challenging conditions or intense competition.

careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in the final hour of the race in 2017, a devastating blow that cost him and his team a shot at the biggest prize in endurance racing.
